description: Conformance fixtures for the .work format. A conformant validator at level n MUST accept every document under valid/ reporting no violations, and MUST reject every document under invalid/ whose rules are at level n or below, reporting exactly the identifiers listed against it. Fixtures above its level are out of scope and MUST be reported as unchecked, never as passed.

levels.1: Structural. Decidable from the document's own bytes, a field at a time.
levels.2: Referential. Decidable from the document as a whole, with references resolved and aggregates recomputed.
levels.3: External. Requires data outside the document: blobs, public keys, EU Trusted Lists, the TIS hierarchy, the provenance log, parent documents.

valid.description: The smallest document that satisfies every rule. One controlled writer, one publisher, one agreement, a PWR link, shares totalling 10000 per right, no content and no signatures.

A work carrying an open infringement claim. A similarity model flagged a bass figure and chord loop pre-release at 0.76, the writer recorded disagreement rather than deleting the flag, and seven months later an estate sent a letter before action. The derivation sits at disposition 'disputed' with a dispute_id, and the dispute records the claim without adjudicating it. Note that clearability reports one_stop true: mandate coverage and legal risk are different questions and a consumer must not read one as the other.

One work, three recordings. A phone demo, a studio master and a licensed cover by another artist, transposed up a fourth and taken at two thirds tempo, all sitting in evidence under one work_id at version 2. The cover shares no spectral content with the master and is still the same work: the matcher attested at 0.91 with a confidence, the writer attested afterwards without one, and the ISWC, the writers and the split are untouched by any of it. The case the format exists to make expressible.

The full worked example. Two writers with only one controlled, a German sub-publisher expressed as include/exclude TIS claims, a cleared interpolation whose consideration does not affect ownership, a split registration outcome, a consent-limited render, publishable fingerprints over the melody and bassline, and a double attestation on the derivation. Carries an @context, so it also exercises JSON-LD compatibility.

invalid.description: Publisher ownership is 4000 rather than 5000, so ownership totals 9000 per right while totals_bps still declares 10000. Two violations from one mutation: the computed total is wrong, and the declared total does not match it.

Credits total correctly at 10000 per right, but totals_bps declares 9000 for pr. Isolates the declared-versus-computed check from the arithmetic check above. A validator that reads the declared total instead of recomputing reports nothing.
publisher_for_writer is empty while a controlled SWR credit exists. There is no chain of title, and the CWR projection would be rejected by the society.
A single credit carries both writer_designation and publisher_type, which describes a composer-publisher. The two CWR vocabularies are distinct and must not be merged.
A derivation at disposition 'disputed' with a null dispute_id and an empty disputes array. The document asserts that someone has made a claim and then says nothing about who, when, or on what basis.

A related_works relation of same_work carrying only a producer attestation. A score of 0.91 is a reason to telephone someone; it is not a finding that two registrations are one asset. The strongest relation a machine may assert is candidate_same_work, and a pipeline permitted to promote its own output will eventually merge two unrelated songs over a shared figure.

A fingerprint declaring disclosure 'exact' over the melody component. An encoding the source can be recovered from intact is a copy of the work, and publishing it under a role described as publishable would disclose the thing the role exists to avoid disclosing. The vocabulary contains 'exact' so that the prohibition has something to name.
